parsed.explanation: Combined regime is uneven. Federal entry and document rules create traveler-facing exposure: binary sex, no X, refusal on discrepancies, possible fraud ineligibility, and hostile immigration/custody practices. Protective division adds shield law, anti-discrimination, state custody congruent, and youth-family protections, materially reducing daily facility/care exposure, especially for minors seeking care. But state law does not pre-empt federal screening, federal facilities, immigration detention, or national counterterrorism framing. Severity if detained remains high; severity at entry is exclusion/stranding. Adult alone and family with minor both face split exposure. Overall sits around elevated risk, slightly above thin hostile jurisdictions because documented traveler-facing protections operate, but below safer states due federal restrictions.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal sex-as-binary rules reject X/new markers and can refuse visas/entry on document, photo or record discrepancies; alleged wilful misrepresentation can trigger permanent inadmissibility. Existing X passports remain valid until expiry.
entry_documents.protection: Court challenges and legal-aid FAQ are pending; some X passports remain valid. State M/F/X documents help only resident/foreign documents if consistent; no documented pre-emption of federal screening.
entry_documents.interaction: State openness does not cancel federal entry cable; mismatched travel papers route to denial/secondary scrutiny.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: If detained or removed through federal immigration/national corrections, documented conversion therapy, hormone removal, forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State/local custody treats gender identity for strip searches and housing; but federal/immigration custody remains hostile.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: State custody protection may not govern federal detention or immigration custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal single-sex rule bars congruent government-funded facilities; many states/provinces have bans, and some criminal trespass. This division is mapped without the listed bans.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State anti-discrimination law and custody/facility practice support identity; shield law and sports ruling.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facilities/funding rules can reach state sites; state protections reduce but do not eliminate exposure.

care_services.exposure: National hostility to youth care, possible insurance reimbursement bar, records subpoenas, and funding restrictions; adult care may face federal sex-binary rules.
care_services.protection: 2022 shield law protects trans patients/providers; state bans service discrimination; minors benefit if seeking lawful care.
care_services.interaction: Shield law offsets home-state bans for visitors, but federal funding/insurance rules may constrain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy names radical pro-trans groups; EO treats gender identity as ideology; border fraud language; foreign advisories; national funding and workplace hostility.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime coverage, anti-discrimination enforcement, local court dismissals for trans athletes; national employment/hate-crime law remains but patchwork.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State-level protective framing coexists with federal threat framing; enforcement uncertainty.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors face national youth-care bans, school/teacher prosecution rhetoric, records exposure and entry mismatch; guardian may be implicated in document screening.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield law, anti-bullying, conversion ban, sports eligibility and M/F/X documents improve minor family care if in state.
minors_guardians.interaction: Visitor minor's exposure depends on whether care/school occurs in protective state and federal funding rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific violence rate documented; national polls show majority support restrictive documents/sports, and other divisions have bathroom criminal trespass.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State public-accommodation non-discrimination, hate-crime coverage, local anti-bullying; functional legal remedies but enforcement not measured.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street risk likely lower here than hostile divisions, but federal hostile climate remains.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unresolved court challenges, inconsistent border officer discretion, federal custody/facility pre-emption, and rubric-based protection not measured in enforcement.
remedies_unknowns.protection: ACL suit, legal-aid FAQ, some EOs blocked/enjoined; state tribunals and shield law offer recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies may mitigate state-level harms but are weaker against entry screening and federal custody.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar border mismatch secondary screening/refusal, but this jurisdiction adds possible permanent fraud bar and severe federal custody; offset by state shield law and non-ban facilities.
Care refusal is corrected quickly in anchor; here care is shielded, but entry screening and federal custody are worse, so overall sits below anchor.
Anchor has charter care protection; this state has shield/care protections, but federal entry/facilities/custody hostile, making combined exposure lower than 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: Traveler first meets national binary/passport rules: mismatch can mean visa denial, long screening, stranding, or if detention occurs federal abuse. Inside protective state, facilities, care, and local custody are largely identity-respecting, and shield law helps visiting families/minors. The two layers interact at borders, federal buildings, immigration, and federally funded services, where state law cannot override. Court cases create uncertainty but no documented pre-emption of federal screening. Thus the combined regime is safer than a hostile state/province but worse than a country with consistent entry/custody protections. Adult alone has elevated risk from entry/custody; minor/guardian has added care-document pressure but shield mitigation.
